statement: There are constants c0, c1 > 0, B < ∞, and a fixed open interval IE containing E, with closure contained in (−2 √ d − 1, 2 √ d − 1), such that the following hold with probability tending to one. 1. After omitting the eigenvalue associated with the constant vector, the ordered eigenvalues are within n−c0 of their Kesten–McKay classical locations. In the normalization above, every eigenvector entry is bounded by a deterministic no(1). 2. Uniformly for ℜζ ∈ IE and S/n ≤ ℑζ ≤ 1, | | | | 1 n Tr(A − ζ)−1 − md(ζ) | | | | ≤ (log n)B( n−c1 + (nℑζ)−c1 ) . Except at at most n1−c1 centers, the resolvent entries on a center and its d neighbors satisfy the same error bound relative to the corresponding infinite d-regular tree entries. These conclusions hold along all admissible n. In particular, #{i : |xi| ≤ S2 } = O(S2 ) on an event of probability tending to one.
